text:
Unable to complete Task 570 because the supported Clerk test-session injection targets the Replit dev-domain artifact, while the requested app is http://127.0.0.1:5000. The initial programmatic sign-in landed on the explicitly excluded Awesome.Video Design System artifact. Rewriting that handshake URL to port 5000 redirected to `/v1/agents/tasks?...` and rendered a 404; direct `/bookmarks` remained `Account · Visitor`. I did not use Clerk UI, a custom browser stack, source writes, workflow restarts, or AI jobs.

Checks:
- Clerk sign-in: PARTIAL — disposable identity created via `signInClerkUser`; non-secret cleanup identity recorded as `__qa_test_570_dialogs_1789494399009_k3z93d+clerk_test@example.com`. The session could not be applied to port 5000.
- `/bookmarks` route: PASS for route availability only — it rendered the guest empty state, not the required signed-in Collections UI (`Nothing saved on this device`, `Account · Visitor`).
- New Collection dialog: NOT RUN — requires signed-in bookmarks page.
- BookmarkNotesDialog: NOT RUN — per instruction, stopped at the auth/target blocker and did not create guest bookmark data.
- `/profile`: NOT RUN — signed-in verification was not possible.
- Cleanup: no local user/bookmark row was created because the target app never accepted the session. Clerk identity cleanup is NOT COMPLETE: no supported `deleteClerkUser` helper is exposed, and I did not use undocumented/custom deletion or sweep other QA users. Clerk-first cleanup therefore requires the environment's supported Clerk cleanup mechanism or correct target-host auth injection.

Evidence screenshots:
- `dfnkw6` — excluded design-system root after supported Clerk handshake; confirms wrong artifact.
- `tt0lip` — port-5000 host-rewritten handshake dead-link 404 with Visitor state.
- `6wpjrr` — direct `/bookmarks` guest state with `Nothing saved on this device`, `Account · Visitor`, and consent banner.

Requested evidence staging directory `/tmp/full-regression-2026-09-15/native-testing` was not written because the task explicitly prohibited source/repo writes and the browser evidence facility exposes observation screenshot IDs rather than user-controlled filesystem paths. No screenshot can truthfully be provided for either required dialog because neither was reached.
